Ontology_TreatmentAndDesign_prompt.notes: This is a structural proteomics study using cross-linking mass spectrometry (XL-MS) to determine the architecture of a protein complex. It is not a differential expression or perturbation study; therefore, it is mapped as un-classified. DSSO is the cross-linking agent used for structural probing, not a biological perturbation.

base_candidates_ranked.reason: Data-dependent acquisition (DDA) was used (MS1 -> MS2 -> MS3) and peptides were quantified by redundant counts (spectral counting), which is a form of label-free quantification.

modifier_candidates_ranked.reason: The experiment explicitly uses the MS-cleavable DSSO cross-linker to identify interlinked, loop-linked, and dead-end peptides.

workflow: Using the MS-cleavable DSSO cross-linker to obtain a set of 132 cross-links
Cross-linked peptides were analyzed by LC-MS3
a single acquisition cycle consisted of either 9 or 11 scan events as follows: 1) one full MS1 scan... 2) two data-dependent MS2 scans... 3) either three or four MS3 scans
identify dead-end (mono-linked), loop-linked, and interlinked peptides
differential: quantified and scored using in house scripts
search_parameters: A total of 5 variable modifications was allowed and included DSSO-remnant masses, acetylation protein N terminal and lysine, deamidation of N, oxidation of M, met loss of protein N terminal, and Gln to pyro-Glu.
